title: Read an Integer From Text

concept.title: A small parser: skip, sign, digits, stop
body: Reading a number out of text follows fixed steps, and an index `i` moves through them: (1) skip the leading spaces, (2) read an optional `+` or `-`, (3) read digits and build the value as `value = value * 10 + digit`, stopping at the first character that is not a digit.

body.code:
i = 0
while i < len(s) and s[i] == " ": i += 1
sign = 1
if i < len(s) and s[i] in "+-":
    sign = -1 if s[i] == "-" else 1
    i += 1
value = 0
while i < len(s) and s[i].isdigit():
    value = value * 10 + int(s[i]); i += 1

body: If the number is too large for a 32-bit signed integer, clamp it: values above 2147483647 become 2147483647 and values below -2147483648 become -2147483648. In C++ and Java stop reading digits once the value is clearly out of range, so that it does not overflow your own variable.

statement: Convert the text at the beginning of a line into an integer. Skip leading spaces; then read an optional sign (+ or -); then read digits until the first character that is not a digit. Ignore the rest of the line. If there are no digits, the result is 0. A result outside the range -2147483648 to 2147483647 is replaced by the nearest border value.
inputFormat: A single line of text (it may start with spaces).
constraints: The line contains letters, digits, spaces and the characters + - .

examples.note: Spaces are skipped, the sign is -, the digits are 42.
The first character is a letter: no digits at the start, so the result is 0.

hints: Use an index that moves forward in three phases: spaces, sign, digits.
Build the value with `value * 10 + digit` and stop at the first non-digit.
Clamp the result to the 32-bit range at the end (and stop early if the value gets huge).

explanation: A single pass with an index through the three phases. The value is clamped at the end, and the digit loop stops early once the value is certainly out of range.

code.python:
s = input()

i = 0
while i < len(s) and s[i] == " ":
    i += 1
sign = 1
if i < len(s) and (s[i] == "+" or s[i] == "-"):
    if s[i] == "-":
        sign = -1
    i += 1
value = 0
while i < len(s) and "0" <= s[i] <= "9":
    value = value * 10 + int(s[i])
    if value > 2147483648:
        break
    i += 1
value *= sign
print(max(-2147483648, min(2147483647, value)))
